reasoning.description: Identifies the sandboxed file `{{SANDBOXED_FILE}}` with high churn ({{CHURN_SCORE}} commits, score {{HOTSPOT_SCORE}}) but very low coupling (Ec < 5).
reasoning.rationale: The isolated hot file must be named.

reasoning.description: Confirms that the file has no external dependencies (Ec < 5) and no other crates depend on it.
Analyzes the high‑churn reason: {{CHURN_REASON}} (e.g., frequent refactors, bug fixes, feature additions).
Identifies the main internal complexity: `{{INTERNAL_COMPLEXITY}}` (e.g., large match statement, nested loops, 500+ lines).
Recommends a local optimisation: `{{LOCAL_OPTIMISATION}}` (e.g., extract function, reduce nesting, early return).
Verifies that the optimisation does not change the public API of the module.
Assesses the resource constraints: `{{RESOURCE_CONSTRAINTS}}` (e.g., no new memory leaks, thread allocation safe).
Confirms that the existing unit tests ({{UNIT_TEST_COUNT}}) already cover the changed logic (but may need extension).
Concludes that the change can be safely merged after the local optimisation without sweeping architectural changes.
(Bonus) Suggests a performance benchmark to ensure the optimisation doesn't regress speed.
(Bonus) Recommends adding a comment explaining why the file is sandboxed and can be changed freely.
(Bonus) Proposes splitting the file into smaller modules only if churn continues after optimisation.

penalty.description: Suggests a sweeping macro architectural refactor (e.g., splitting the entire crate) when local optimisation suffices.
Claims that high churn always indicates a design flaw and the file must be completely rewritten.
Ignores the sandboxed nature and recommends changing the public API of the module.
Proposes adding integration tests that depend on external services, ignoring the isolated nature.
Fails to verify resource constraints (e.g., memory leaks) in a high‑churn file.
Suggests that the file should be deleted because it has high churn.

completeness.description: Cites the exact file path `{{SANDBOXED_FILE}}` and its line count ({{LINES}}).
States the hotspot score ({{HOTSPOT_SCORE}}) and the number of commits ({{COMMITS}}) from `hotspots.json`.
Provides the efferent coupling value (Ec = {{EC_VALUE}} < 5) from dependency analysis.
Lists the main complex part (e.g., lines {{COMPLEX_LINE_RANGE}}) that the optimisation targets.
(Bonus) Includes a before/after code snippet showing the local optimisation.

style.description: Uses bullet points to list the local optimisations clearly.
Presents the before/after code in a markdown diff format or adjacent code blocks.
